A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete, readable scientific material. All 27 appendix pages match after accounting for pagination; v2 chiefly adds a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical constructions, regret bounds, and proofs, including Appendices A–C. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the same theoretical content without adding empirical results. Checklist items 4–8 explicitly confirm that the paper contains no experiments.

M1.justification: The two-node LM-MASSP construction, linear transition features, uniform costs, and optimal-policy characterization in Sections 2–4 are unchanged. No algorithmic component or procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation scenarios. The unchanged hard-instance family is a theoretical construction.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparator algorithms. Section 1.1 and Table 1 retain the same comparisons with published theoretical regret bounds.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols or settings. The added checklist confirms their absence without introducing evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, error analyses, or case studies are added or removed. The existing analytical discussion and proof appendices are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Checklist item 7 marks experimental statistical significance as not applicable.

E6.justification: Table 1, the stated regret bounds, and all other mathematical findings are unchanged. No empirical result entries are introduced.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorems 1–2, supporting lemmas and corollaries, and all derivations in Appendices A–C are identical. The appendix shifts from pages 13–39 to pages 19–45 without mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 6 retain the same claims about the first decentralized MASSP regret lower bound, hard-instance construction, and symmetry-based characterization of optimal policies.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the same applicability caveats, empirical-validation difficulties, and open directions. Checklist item 2 points to existing assumptions and limitations; its generic resource-utilization benefit adds no substantive scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: No implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, or reproduction instructions change. The checklist confirms the absence of experiments and released assets without introducing resources or changing access.

R1.justification: The same 27 references, related-work discussion, and research positioning are retained. The checklist's administrative guideline links do not add research comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a NeurIPS checklist between the references and appendices, updates the publication notice, and changes the funding name from Alpha to ALFA. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds checklist pages with a numbered question-and-answer layout and shortens the first-page publication footer. Table 1 and the existing scientific page layouts remain unchanged; no scientific figures or tables are added or redesigned.

improvement.justification: The main text, Table 1, and complete proof appendices retain the same scientific content and explanatory quality. The checklist adds mainly administrative disclosure, while item 15 introduces an apparent missing 'not' about human-subjects research, contradicting item 14. These peripheral changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
